THE UI BUTTON DECEPTION: PROMPTS ARE NEVER IN GOOGLE DRIVE TRASH Look closely at Google’s own user interface dialogs: Google AI Studio claims: “Move prompt to trash… Your prompt will be permanently deleted after 30 days.” Google Drive claims upon permanent deletion: “The item will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered later. This action cannot be undone.” Here is the undeniable technical contradiction: PROMPTS AND CONVERSATIONS ARE NEVER STORED IN GOOGLE DRIVE TRASH IN THE FIRST PLACE. Only the tiny client-side JSON pointer/metadata file is moved to Google Drive Trash. The actual prompt, full conversation history, and model states reside exclusively on Google’s backend servers (API Storage). The UI deliberately deceives the user into believing that the “prompt” itself is being placed into the trash and destroyed, while in reality, the backend data is never touched or purged by the Drive Trash action. Slapping a “P4” (Eventual / Lowest Priority) and “S4” (Minimal Impact) rating onto Issue #552682596 while the UI actively misrepresents where and how prompts are deleted is textbook corporate bad faith: Google officially verified the defect (TRIAGED), knows the deletion dialogs are factually misleading, and deliberately chooses to leave this deceptive architecture active!
